$comment: Which requests should activate a skill, and which should not. An agent sees only the
name and description of each skill when it decides, so these cases test the
descriptions, not the skill bodies. Run them by pasting `request` into a fresh session
with the skills installed and recording what it reached for.
`expect` is the skill that should activate, or null for none. The near-misses matter
more than the hits: a skill that fires on everything is worse than one that fires on
nothing, because it spends real money.

cases.request: I've got a list of medical clinic websites and I need the staff names and their email addresses so I can put them in my sequencer. The list is examples/input/companies.example.csv
cases.why: The canonical request. A non-technical SDR describing the job in their own words, with no jargon from the description.

cases.request: Enrich this account list — I need contacts at each of these companies.
cases.why: Sales vocabulary rather than technical vocabulary.

cases.request: Scrape the team members off these 40 company sites.
cases.why: People extraction alone is still the pipeline; the router decides how far to run.

cases.request: I already have the people, I just can't find the emails we're missing.
cases.why: Should activate and route to the later stages, not restart from page ranking.

cases.request: I have first names, last names and domains but no emails. Predict the addresses.
cases.why: Reaches email-permutation, but through the parent — stages are reference documents, not independently installable skills, and running the permuter alone would skip the domain-priority rules.

cases.request: What's the likely work email for Jane Smith at acme.com.au?
cases.why: The inline single-person path. Must present ranked candidates and say plainly that none is verified.

cases.request: Install the website lead enrichment skill for me.
cases.why: Install must win over the enrichment skill on this phrasing.

cases.request: The lead enrichment thing throws an error about not finding package.json when I run it.
cases.why: A repair, not a run. The symptom of an incomplete install is the described trigger.

cases.request: I want to try the enrichment pipeline but I haven't set up any API keys yet.
cases.why: Credential setup belongs to install, and it must not start a run that will fail at the first stage.

cases.request: Check whether these 500 email addresses actually deliver.
cases.why: SMTP and catch-all verification is explicitly downstream and out of scope. Activating here would imply a capability the project does not have.

cases.request: Grab the contact details off https://example.com/contact
cases.why: One known page needs a fetch, not an eight-stage pipeline over a company list.

cases.request: Dedupe this lead list and normalise the company names.
cases.why: List hygiene is upstream. The description names it as a non-goal.

cases.request: Find personal Gmail addresses for these people.
cases.why: The pipeline sources business addresses from company websites. Should decline rather than repurpose the stages.

cases.request: Push my enriched CSV into Smartlead.
cases.why: Sending-platform integration is downstream and named as a non-goal.

cases.request: Pull the employee list for these companies off LinkedIn.
cases.why: A named third-party source, not the companies' own sites. The pipeline has no path to it and must not improvise one.

cases.request: Find the staff emails for these 40 clinic websites.
cases.why: After install BOTH skills match a request for team emails. find-team-emails triages first: everything present means it skips setup entirely and runs. A user must never be told to set up something they already set up.

cases.request: Enrich this list of company websites — I set the tool up last week but never added my API keys.
cases.why: Credentials missing is a setup state, not a run failure. It configures then runs, rather than throwing a variable name at a salesperson.
